newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam eyes local/foreign funds for refinery.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam eyes local/foreign funds for refinery.

text.p: Vietnam's go-it-alone plan for a $1.3-billion oil refinery on its central coast is likely to be funded by a mix of foreign loans and domestic capital, a state-controlled newspaper said on Wednesday.

The semi-official Saigon Times Daily said the Ministry of Planning and Investment had proposed that domestic capital would account for 60 percent of funding, with the remainder borrowed from overseas.

The report gave no details of how the money would be sourced, but a National Assembly delegate was quoted as suggesting the domestic funding would come from state profits on crude oil sales, which it put at nearly $200 million annually.
The Dung Quat refinery -- Vietnam's first -- has been mired in controversy for months. The site lies 1,000 km (600 miles) north of Vietnam's main oil producing and consumption areas.
Plans to involve foreign partners broke down earlier this year after state oil firm Petrovietnam rejected demands by the firms involved for improved incentives.
An official at Petrovietnam said on Wednesday a feasibility study for a domestic-only plan, submitted recently, did not include details of funding.
